tenant.summary: Landlords must return the security deposit within a reasonable period after move-out, minus legitimate deductions (damage beyond normal wear, unpaid dues).
next_steps: Send a written demand letter (email/registered post) requesting the deposit within 15 days
Keep photos/videos of the property condition at move-out
If unresolved, file a complaint with the Rent Authority / Rent Court set up under the state tenancy act
Consumer/civil court is an option if amount is disputed and Rent Authority is unavailable
tenant.escalation_path: Rent Authority (or Rent Court) under the applicable State Tenancy Act

consumer.summary: Consumers who receive defective goods or deficient services can seek replacement, repair, refund, or compensation.
next_steps: Raise the complaint with the seller/service provider in writing first
If unresolved within a reasonable time, file a complaint on the National Consumer Helpline / e-Daakhil portal
Claims under ₹50 lakh generally go to the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
consumer.escalation_path: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission / e-Daakhil portal

workplace.summary: Employees are entitled to timely payment of wages, safe working conditions, and protection from arbitrary termination without due process (subject to employment terms/state law).
next_steps: Raise the issue in writing with HR/employer and keep a copy
If wages are withheld, file a claim with the Labour Commissioner's office
For unfair termination, consult the local Labour Court / Industrial Tribunal

default.summary: This specific dispute type isn't in our grounded knowledge base yet — general guidance only, please verify with a legal aid clinic (e.g. District Legal Services Authority, DLSA) before acting.
next_steps: Contact your District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) for free legal aid
Call the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) helpline: 15100
